bullets: **Ecosystem** = all living organisms in an area + the non-living environment. **Biotic:** plants, animals, microbes. **Abiotic:** temperature, rainfall, wind, soil, minerals.
Natural ecosystems: forests, ponds, lakes. Artificial ecosystems: gardens, crop fields, aquariums.
**Producers** (green plants) → **consumers** (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, parasites) → **decomposers** (bacteria, fungi) return nutrients to the soil.
Each step of a food chain is a **trophic level**: grass (producer) → grasshopper (primary consumer) → frog (secondary) → snake (tertiary) → eagle.
Green plants capture about **1%** of the sunlight falling on their leaves.
**10 per cent law:** only about 10% of the energy is passed to the next level. The rest is used for life processes or lost as heat.
So food chains have only **3–4 levels**, and there are fewer organisms at higher levels.
Energy flow is **unidirectional**: it never goes back to the previous level. Food chains interconnect to form a **food web**.

box: **Biological magnification:** non-biodegradable chemicals (e.g. pesticides) are not broken down, so they build up at each trophic level. Their concentration is highest at the **top** of the food chain, including in humans.

bullets: Ozone (O_{3}) in the upper atmosphere shields the Earth from harmful **UV radiation** (which causes skin cancer).
Formation: O_{2} → O + O (UV splits oxygen); then O + O_{2} → O_{3}
Depleted by **CFCs** (used in refrigerants and fire extinguishers). In 1987, UNEP got countries to agree to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels. Now CFC-free refrigerators are made.

table: Not broken down; stays for a long time
Peels, paper, wood, cotton, food waste
Plastic, polythene, glass, DDT, some metals

bullets: Reduce waste: segregate wet and dry, compost kitchen waste, carry cloth bags, avoid single-use plastic, reuse, recycle.
Even biodegradable options have costs: kulhads (clay cups) on trains would use up fertile top soil, so paper cups are used.
